title: Autologous T Cells Genetically Engineered to Express Drug-Regulatable, Inducible, and Membrane-Bound Interleukin 12 (DRIM-IL-12) and T-Cell Receptors Against Neoantigens (e.g., KRAS, p53) in Metastatic Solid Tumors
official: Phase I/II Study of Autologous T-Cells Genetically Engineered to Express Drug-Regulatable, Inducible, and Membrane-Bound Interleukin 12 (DRIM-IL-12) and T-Cell Receptors Against Neoantigens (e.g., KRAS, or p53) in Metastatic Solid Tumors
summary:
Background:

Solid tumor cancers account for more than 90% of cancer-related deaths. They include cancers that affect organs such as the breast, lungs, stomach, intestines, and liver. Researchers want to try a new kind of treatment: a therapy that changes the genes of a person s own immune cells (white blood cells called T cells) so they will be better at recognizing and attacking cancer cells.

Objective:

To learn if T cells with changed genes can make tumors smaller in people with solid tumor cancers in a safe way.

Eligibility:

People aged 18 to 72 years with a solid tumor cancer that has spread to other parts of the body and has not responded to treatment.

Design:

Some participants may need to be screened. They will have blood tests and tests of their heart and lung function. They will have imaging scans. Photos will be taken of their body.

Participants will undergo leukapheresis: Blood will be taken from the body through a needle inserted into a vein. The blood will pass through a machine that separates out the T cells. The remaining blood will be returned to the body through a different needle. The collected T cells will be genetically modified in a lab.

Participants will check in to the hospital. They will receive drugs to prepare their body for the treatment. Then the modified T cells will be infused through a needle inserted into a vein. They will stay in the hospital until they are well enough to go home. This may be 1 to 2 weeks.

Follow-up will continue for 3 years, but participants will need to stay in touch with the gene therapy team for 15 years.
criteria:
* INCLUSION CRITERIA:
* Individuals must have histologically or cytologically confirmed Metastatic, solid cancer falls into one of three cohorts: (1) gastrointestinal (GI) and genitourinary (GU) cancers; (2) breast, ovarian, and other solid cancers; (3) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) confirmed by the NCI Laboratory of Pathology.

NOTE: NSCLC includes but is not limited to squamous cell carcinoma, adenosquamous carcinoma, or adenocarcinomas.

* Individuals must have measurable disease per RECIST 1.1.
* Refractory to approved standard systemic therapy. Specifically:

  * Participants with metastatic colorectal cancer must have received oxaliplatin or irinotecan.
  * Participants with breast and ovarian cancer must be refractory to first-line treatment and refractory to or have refused second-line treatments.
  * Participants with NSCLC must have received at least one platinum-based chemotherapy regimen OR an FDA-approved targeted therapy (e.g. EGFR-directed therapy), when appropriate.
* Participants with three (3) or fewer brain metastases that are \< 1 cm in diameter and asymptomatic are eligible. Lesions that have been treated with stereotactic radiosurgery must be clinically stable for two weeks after treatment for the participant to be eligible. Participants with surgically resected brain metastases are eligible. As noted below, participants must be stable without the use of systemic steroids.
* Age \>= 18 years and \<= 72 years.
* Clinical performance status of Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) 0 or 1.
* Women of child-bearing potential (WOCBP) must agree to use highly effective contraception (hormonal, intrauterine device \[IUD\], surgical sterilization) or practice abstinence starting at the time of study entry, for the duration of study therapy, and 12 months after the last dose of combined chemotherapy.

NOTE: WOCBP is defined as any person assigned female at birth who has experienced menarche and who has not undergone successful surgical sterilization or who is not postmenopausal.

Men able to father a child must agree to use an effective method of contraception (barrier, surgical sterilization, abstinence) for the duration of the study treatment and for 4 months after the last dose of combined chemotherapy. We also will recommend these individuals with partners of childbearing potential ask partners to be on highly effective birth control (hormonal, intrauterine device (IUD), surgical sterilization) or to practice abstinence. Men must not freeze or donate sperm within the same period.

-Nursing participants must be willing to discontinue nursing through 4 months after the last dose of the study drug(s).

Serology

* Seronegative for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibody
* Seronegative for hepatitis B antigen (HBV), and seronegative for hepatitis C (HCV) antibody. If hepatitis C antibody test is positive, then participant must be tested for the presence of antigen by real time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and be HCV ribonucleic acid (RNA) negative.

Hematology

* Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) \> 1000/mm\^3 without the support of filgrastim
* White Blood Cell (WBC) \>= 2500/mm\^3
* Platelet count \>= 80,000/mm\^3
* Hemoglobin \> 8.0 g/dL. Subjects may be transfused to reach this cut-off.

Chemistry

* Serum ALT/AST \<= 5.0 x upper limit of normal (ULN)
* Serum creatinine \<= 1.6 mg/dL
* Total bilirubin \<= 2.0 mg/dL, except in participants with Gilbert s Syndrome, who must have a total bilirubin \< 3.0 mg/dL.
* Participants must have completed any prior systemic therapy at the time of enrollment.

NOTE: Participants may have undergone minor surgical procedures or limited field radiotherapy within the four weeks prior to initiation of study intervention, as long as related major organ toxicities have recovered to grade 1 or less.

* For participants with NSCLC: More than two weeks must have elapsed since any prior palliation for major bronchial occlusion or bleeding at the time the participant receives the preparative regimen, and participant s toxicities must have recovered to a grade 1 or less.
* Ability of participant to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.
* Subjects must be co-enrolled on protocol 03C0277, Cell Harvest and Preparation for Surgery Branch Treatment Protocols.

EXCLUSION CRITERIA:

* Women who are pregnant. NOTE: Certain malignancies may secrete hormones that produce false positive pregnancy tests. Serial blood testing (e.g. human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG) measurements) and/ or ultrasound may be performed for clarification.
* Concurrent systemic steroid therapy.
* Active systemic infections requiring anti-infective treatment, coagulation disorders, or any other active or uncompensated major medical illnesses. Participants with cancer-associated deep vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism may still be eligible pending overall assessment.
* For participants with NSCLC : Any major bronchial occlusion or bleeding not amenable to palliation.
* Any form of primary immunodeficiency (such as Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease and Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome \[AIDS\]).
* History of major organ autoimmune disease or major organ autoimmune toxicity associated with prior therapy, excluding resolved skin or thyroid toxicities.
* Concurrent opportunistic infections
* Concurrent major medical illnesses (including but not limited to unpalliated biliary or bowel occlusion, cholangitis, or digestive tract bleeding)
* History of severe immediate hypersensitivity reaction to cyclophosphamide, fludarabine, or lenalidomide.
* History of coronary revascularization or ischemic symptoms.
* For select participants with a clinical history prompting cardiac evaluation: last known left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) \<= 45%.
* For select participants with a clinical history prompting pulmonary evaluation: known forced expiratory volume (FEV1) \<= 50% predicted.
* Individuals that require thalidomide analogs or ubiquitin-proteosome inhibitors for management of concurrent disease.
* Individuals who are receiving any other investigational agents.
